quests.hint: Go away from a place to head somewhere else.
quests.explanation: We leave a place without a preposition: 'leave home', 'leave the office'. 'Go out of the house' is possible, but 'leave' is the natural everyday verb for departing.
quests.textToSpeak: The film starts at eight, so we should ___ home by seven at the latest.
quests.correctAnswer: The film starts at eight, so we should leave home by seven at the latest.
quests.contextClue: The film's start time forces the group to depart earlier.

quests.hint: Ask people to come to something you are organising.
quests.explanation: 'Invite' takes the person as its object: 'invite my classmates'. The event follows with 'to': 'invite them to the party'.
quests.textToSpeak: We're having a party on Saturday, and I want to ___ all my old classmates.
quests.correctAnswer: We're having a party on Saturday, and I want to invite all my old classmates.
quests.contextClue: A party needs guests, so the speaker must ask people to attend.

quests.hint: You did not remember to do something you meant to do.
quests.explanation: 'Forget to + verb' means you did not do the thing: 'I forgot to lock the door'. The forms are irregular: forget, forgot, forgotten.
quests.textToSpeak: I think I ___ to lock the front door. Can we go back and check?
quests.correctAnswer: I think I forgot to lock the front door. Can we go back and check?
quests.contextClue: Going back to 'check' suggests a possible mistake that already happened.

quests.hint: The opposite of cold, and the reason for the warning.
quests.explanation: 'Hot' describes high temperature in food, drinks, weather and objects. 'Warm' is milder, so 'hot' is what we use for a warning.
quests.textToSpeak: Careful, the soup just came off the stove and it's very ___.
quests.correctAnswer: Careful, the soup just came off the stove and it's very hot.
quests.contextClue: 'Just came off the stove' tells you the temperature.

quests.hint: Not wide; there is very little space from one side to the other.
quests.explanation: Narrow is the opposite of wide and is often used for roads, doors, bridges and gaps. 'So + adjective + that' links a quality to its result.
quests.textToSpeak: The street is so ___ that two cars can't pass each other.
quests.correctAnswer: The street is so narrow that two cars can't pass each other.
quests.contextClue: Two cars cannot pass, so the width of the street is the problem.

quests.hint: It feels good to sit in and doesn't hurt you.
quests.explanation: Say it as three or four syllables, 'KUMF-ter-bul' is common in speech. We use it for furniture, clothes and shoes: 'a comfortable chair'.
quests.textToSpeak: My new chair is very ___, so I can work for hours without a sore back.
quests.correctAnswer: My new chair is very comfortable, so I can work for hours without a sore back.
quests.contextClue: Working for hours without a sore back is a result of how the chair feels.

quests.hint: A time word meaning 'up to the moment when'.
quests.explanation: After 'until' we use the present simple to talk about the future: 'until I get back', not 'until I will get back'.
quests.textToSpeak: Don't start the film ___ I get back from the shop. I want to watch it too.
quests.correctAnswer: Don't start the film until I get back from the shop. I want to watch it too.
quests.contextClue: The speaker asks for a delay that ends when they return.

quests.hint: It marks the starting point of a range.
quests.explanation: 'From... to...' marks the start and end of a period: 'from nine to five', 'from Monday to Friday'.
quests.textToSpeak: The shop is open ___ nine to five, Monday to Friday.
quests.correctAnswer: The shop is open from nine to five, Monday to Friday.
quests.contextClue: Both 'to five' and 'to Friday' show that two limits are being given.

quests.hint: An adverb that shows surprise something happened sooner than expected.
quests.explanation: 'Already' shows something happened earlier than expected. In a surprised question it comes at the end: 'Finished already?'
quests.textToSpeak: You're finished ___? I only gave you the file ten minutes ago.
quests.correctAnswer: You're finished already? I only gave you the file ten minutes ago.
quests.contextClue: 'Only... ten minutes ago' creates the feeling of surprise.

quests.hint: Small, medium and large are all examples of this.
quests.explanation: In shops we ask for a size: 'What size are you?', 'Do you have it in a smaller size?'. The comparative comes before the noun: 'a larger size'.
quests.textToSpeak: Do you have this shirt in a larger ___?
quests.correctAnswer: Do you have this shirt in a larger size?
quests.contextClue: 'Larger' needs a noun that names something measurable about clothes.

quests.hint: A period when a shop sells things at a lower price.
quests.explanation: In American English 'on sale' usually means the price has been reduced, while British speakers often say 'in the sale'. Both describe reduced prices.
quests.textToSpeak: This coat is on ___ this week, so it's thirty percent cheaper.
quests.correctAnswer: This coat is on sale this week, so it's thirty percent cheaper.
quests.contextClue: 'Thirty percent cheaper' explains the special situation.

quests.hint: Notes and coins.
quests.explanation: 'Cash' is uncountable: 'pay in cash', 'I don't have any cash'. It is usually contrasted with 'card'.
quests.textToSpeak: Sorry, our card machine isn't working today, so we can only accept ___.
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry, our card machine isn't working today, so we can only accept cash.
quests.contextClue: When cards can't be used, only one other way to pay remains.

quests.hint: All the cars, vans and lorries moving on a road.
quests.explanation: Traffic is uncountable: 'a lot of traffic', 'heavy traffic'. We don't say 'a traffic' or 'traffics'.
quests.textToSpeak: There's a lot of ___ on the main road this morning, so the bus is crawling.
quests.correctAnswer: There's a lot of traffic on the main road this morning, so the bus is crawling.
quests.contextClue: A bus moving very slowly means the road is full of something.

quests.hint: Not on time; later than planned.
quests.explanation: This is a passive form: 'was delayed'. To measure the extra time we use 'by': 'delayed by forty minutes'.
quests.textToSpeak: The train was ___ by forty minutes because of a signal problem.
quests.correctAnswer: The train was delayed by forty minutes because of a signal problem.
quests.contextClue: 'By forty minutes' measures the lateness, and the signal problem gives the cause.

quests.hint: The raised area beside the tracks where passengers wait.
quests.explanation: Stations use numbered platforms: 'platform four'. In questions the preposition stays at the end: 'Which platform does it leave from?'
quests.textToSpeak: Excuse me, which ___ does the train to Leeds leave from?
quests.correctAnswer: Excuse me, which platform does the train to Leeds leave from?
quests.contextClue: The traveller needs a numbered place inside the station.

quests.hint: After 'would you mind', use the -ing form of the verb that means 'say again'.
quests.explanation: 'Would you mind + -ing' is a polite way to ask someone for a favour: 'Would you mind opening the window?'
quests.textToSpeak: Sorry, the music is so loud that I missed that. Would you mind ___ it?
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry, the music is so loud that I missed that. Would you mind repeating it?
quests.contextClue: 'Would you mind' must be followed by an -ing verb.

quests.hint: To get the meaning of something in your mind.
quests.explanation: Understand is irregular: understand, understood, understood. It is rarely used in continuous forms; we say 'I understand', not 'I am understanding'.
quests.textToSpeak: I've read this sentence three times and I still don't ___ it.
quests.correctAnswer: I've read this sentence three times and I still don't understand it.
quests.contextClue: Three attempts to read without success point to a lack of meaning.

quests.hint: Make something go from you to another person.
quests.explanation: 'Send' takes the thing and often the person: 'send it', 'send me the file'. It is irregular: send, sent, sent.
quests.textToSpeak: The email didn't arrive. Could you ___ it again, please?
quests.correctAnswer: The email didn't arrive. Could you send it again, please?
quests.contextClue: If something did not arrive, the action has to be done again.

quests.hint: What you do when two people haven't met before.
quests.explanation: We introduce someone TO another person: 'Let me introduce you to Lucas.' Introducing yourself uses 'myself': 'I'd like to introduce myself.'
quests.textToSpeak: Come over here. Let me ___ you to my friend Lucas.
quests.correctAnswer: Come over here. Let me introduce you to my friend Lucas.
quests.contextClue: A named friend and 'come over here' show two people meeting for the first time.

quests.hint: The small word that links 'congratulations' to the good news.
quests.explanation: 'Congratulations on' is the standard pattern: 'on your promotion', 'on the wedding'. 'For' is not the standard choice here.
quests.textToSpeak: Congratulations ___ your new job! When do you start?
quests.correctAnswer: Congratulations on your new job! When do you start?
quests.contextClue: The new job is the reason for the celebration.

quests.hint: Come along and become part of a group.
quests.explanation: Join takes a direct object with no 'to': 'join us', not 'join to us'. You can also 'join a club' or 'join a class'.
quests.textToSpeak: We're going hiking on Sunday. Why don't you ___ us?
quests.correctAnswer: We're going hiking on Sunday. Why don't you join us?
quests.contextClue: 'Why don't you...' is an invitation to be part of the group's plan.

quests.hint: A common illness that makes you sneeze.
quests.explanation: For common illnesses we use 'have' or 'get': 'have a cold', 'get a cold'. In this meaning cold is countable.
quests.textToSpeak: I've got a terrible ___, with a runny nose and a sore throat.
quests.correctAnswer: I've got a terrible cold, with a runny nose and a sore throat.
quests.contextClue: Runny nose and sore throat are the usual signs of one illness.

quests.hint: An unpleasant feeling in your body when something hurts.
quests.explanation: 'Pain' is uncountable in general, but 'a pain in my knee' is common for a specific place. It works well with 'sharp' or 'dull'.
quests.textToSpeak: I get a sharp ___ in my knee when I go up the stairs.
quests.correctAnswer: I get a sharp pain in my knee when I go up the stairs.
quests.contextClue: 'Sharp' before the blank and 'in my knee' after it describe a physical sensation.

quests.hint: Two times.
quests.explanation: For frequency we say 'once', 'twice', then 'three times', 'four times'. 'Twice' replaces 'two times' in normal speech.
quests.textToSpeak: Take this medicine ___ a day, once in the morning and once at night.
quests.correctAnswer: Take this medicine twice a day, once in the morning and once at night.
quests.contextClue: 'Once... and once' adds up to a number.

quests.hint: Use a hot flat tool to make clothes smooth.
quests.explanation: Iron is both a noun ('an iron') and a verb ('to iron a shirt'). It is pronounced 'EYE-urn', with the r before the n.
quests.textToSpeak: This shirt is full of creases. I need to ___ it before the interview.
quests.correctAnswer: This shirt is full of creases. I need to iron it before the interview.
quests.contextClue: Creases before an important event mean the shirt has to be smoothed.

quests.hint: Put things back where they belong so a place looks neat.
quests.explanation: 'Tidy up' is a phrasal verb: 'tidy up the room' or 'tidy the room up'. Tidy is also an adjective, as in 'a tidy desk'.
quests.textToSpeak: Your room is a mess. Please ___ it up before your friends come.
quests.correctAnswer: Your room is a mess. Please tidy it up before your friends come.
quests.contextClue: 'A mess' is the problem, and the visitors are the reason to fix it.

quests.hint: Take everything out of a container so nothing is left.
quests.explanation: Empty is both an adjective ('an empty bin') and a verb ('to empty the bin'). As a verb it means to remove what is inside.
quests.textToSpeak: The bin is full, so I'll ___ it before I go to bed.
quests.correctAnswer: The bin is full, so I'll empty it before I go to bed.
quests.contextClue: A full container leads to the opposite state.

quests.hint: Decide that a planned event will not take place.
quests.explanation: You can cancel a match, a flight, a meeting or an order. 'Might + base verb' expresses possibility: 'might cancel'.
quests.textToSpeak: The rain is getting worse, so they might ___ the match.
quests.correctAnswer: The rain is getting worse, so they might cancel the match.
quests.contextClue: Worsening rain is a reason why the plan could stop.

quests.hint: Put a question to someone.
quests.explanation: 'Ask' takes the person directly: 'ask your teacher', not 'ask to your teacher'. Pattern: ask + person + question.
quests.textToSpeak: If you don't know the answer, just ___ your teacher. She'll be happy to help.
quests.correctAnswer: If you don't know the answer, just ask your teacher. She'll be happy to help.
quests.contextClue: The teacher has the answer, and 'happy to help' shows she is willing.

quests.hint: Look at two or more things to see which is cheaper or better.
quests.explanation: We compare prices, options or products. The noun is 'comparison', and 'compare A with B' is a common pattern.
quests.textToSpeak: Before buying anything online, I always ___ prices on a few different websites.
quests.correctAnswer: Before buying anything online, I always compare prices on a few different websites.
quests.contextClue: Checking 'a few different websites' means looking at several options.
